note: config_evpn side B, rebound to the independent EVPN lexicon (lb.*) for E1.

concepts.label: evpn-instance
concepts.gloss: the EVPN instance (MAC-VRF) realising the customer's Ethernet service across the PEs
concepts.example: EVI 5000 (MAC-VRF ACME) on PE1, PE2, PE3

concepts.label: attachment-circuit
concepts.gloss: the interface on a PE where a customer site attaches to the EVI
concepts.example: ge-0/0/4 on PE1 bound to EVI 5000

concepts.label: vpn-network-access
concepts.gloss: the per-PE endpoint of the EVI at an attachment circuit

concepts.label: bridge-domain
concepts.gloss: the bridge domain (VLAN) of the MAC-VRF, one broadcast domain across the EVI

concepts.label: ingress-policer
concepts.gloss: the ingress policer applied on an attachment circuit to enforce the committed rate

concepts.label: traffic-class
concepts.gloss: the forwarding class applied to frames in the EVI

concepts.label: mac-vrf-learning
concepts.gloss: how the MAC-VRF learns local customer MACs on an attachment circuit before advertising them in BGP
concepts.example: local learning on AC-PE1, then EVPN type-2 advertisement

concepts.label: interface-mtu
concepts.gloss: the L2 MTU enforced on the attachment circuit and core

concepts.label: ethernet-segment
concepts.gloss: the Ethernet Segment: the set of links by which a multi-homed site attaches to more than one PE, identified by an ESI (network-side self-extension; no single-homed MEF counterpart)
concepts.example: ESI 00:11:...:01 for a dual-homed site on PE2 and PE3

concepts.label: MAC-mobility
concepts.gloss: the EVPN mechanism handling a customer MAC that moves between attachment points, using a sequence number (network-side self-extension)
concepts.example: sequence bump when a MAC moves from PE1 to PE2
instances: mobility seq=3 for a moved MAC
